contributions: Characterizes reasoning length dynamics under stepwise truncation and names thinking-content compensation: insufficient thinking is compensated by longer content, until content length saturates into a narrow band and further thinking adds only redundancy.

Characterizes reasoning semantic dynamics by sampling content continuations at each truncation step and measuring D_global(k) = KL(Q_k || Q_inf) in PCA space, showing an early high-drift exploration phase followed by convergence into a stable basin with repetitive oscillation rather than collapse to a point.

Defines the Reasoning Completion Point as the earliest step at which content-length stabilization and semantic convergence hold simultaneously, giving an instance-specific stopping criterion rather than a fixed budget.

Identifies a sharp drop in the rank of the </think> token as an online, answer-format-invariant signature that coincides with first answer emergence, and distills offline RCP labels into deterministic rank-based stopping rules (RCPD) requiring no training and no extra forward passes.

Shows against an iso-compute-calibrated Budget Force baseline that where a trace is cut matters more than how much is cut, and reports a counterfactual injection experiment in which 49 of 64 trials adopt an injected wrong intermediate answer, evidence that post-RCP computation rationalizes rather than re-verifies.
limitations:
Stated: the analysis and evaluation cover reasoning models from the Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1 families only, chosen because they expose explicit thinking delimiters and the decoding signals RCPD needs; closed-source APIs, tool-augmented agents and multimodal models were not tested, so how universal RCP-like phase transitions are is left open.

Not stated, and worth noticing. (1) The offline definition and the deployed detector are never checked against each other: RCPD is validated only end-to-end on accuracy and tokens, and the paper reports no precision, recall or step-level error of RCPD's trigger against its own gold k_RCP labels. A detector that ignored k_RCP but stopped at a reasonable place would produce the same Table 1. (2) The formal apparatus (Gaussian fit in r-dimensional PCA space, KL residual, Mahalanobis basin) does not survive into the deployed method, which is four hand-set rank thresholds -- R_t <= 5, the ladder [10, 50, 100, 1000], <= 20 over 3 steps, <= 50 over 6 steps -- with no sensitivity analysis and no statement of how they transfer across models, though they were fit on Math-500 alone and applied unchanged to AIME and GPQA-D. (3) The sample count for the semantic probe is written as M in Section 3.1 and N in Eq. 3 and its value is never given in this version, so the semantic analysis is not reproducible as written. (4) AIME24 and AIME25 have 30 problems each; no seed count, variance or confidence interval is reported anywhere, so several-point differences between methods rest on one or two problems. (5) RPCR places tokens in the denominator, so among methods that hold accuracy the most compressive one wins close to by construction; worse, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B has no No-Think mode and its RPCR is computed against the Qwen3-8B No-Think baseline, making that column not comparable with the others. (6) No wall-clock measurement is reported, only token counts, although RCPD queries the next-token distribution and evaluates rules at every sentence boundary. (7) The consistent GPQA-D accuracy gain under aggressive truncation is compatible with the overthinking account but also with a multiple-choice artifact, and is not separated.
method:
Generation is formalized as a coupling of a thinking process t and a content process y, P(y,t|x) = P(t|x)P(y|x,t). Both are segmented into sentence-level reasoning steps via NLTK. The central instrument is a stepwise truncation protocol: for each step k the thinking trajectory is cut after s_k and the end-of-thinking delimiter (e.g. </think>) is force-injected, so the model must produce content from the prefix t_{1:k}, giving y_k ~ P(y | x, t_{1:k}). Two lenses are then applied to the resulting family of truncated runs.

Reasoning Length Dynamics tracks Thinking Length L_t = k against Content Length L_c (steps in the induced content) and answer correctness across k. This exposes thinking-content compensation (early on, insufficient thinking is offloaded into longer content, and incorrect answers cluster at short content) followed by thinking redundancy (content length collapses into a narrow band and stays constant even as k grows by over 100 steps).

Reasoning Semantic Dynamics probes the same truncation family semantically. For each prefix the paper independently samples multiple content continuations (denoted {y_k^(i)}, written with sample count M in Section 3.1 and N in Eq. 3; the numeric value is not stated in this version), embeds each with the Qwen3 Embedding model, and performs PCA over the pooled embeddings. A 2D projection is used only for visualization; the quantitative analysis projects to an r-dimensional PCA space (r >> 2) and approximates the induced distribution as a Gaussian Q_k = N(mu_k, Sigma_k) with Sigma_k = Cov({z_k^(i)}) + lambda*I for numerical stability. A terminal reference Q_inf is estimated by pooling samples from a short tail window of the final truncation steps, and the global convergence residual is D_global(k) = D_KL(Q_k || Q_inf).

The two lenses are combined into a definition. Content stabilization is Delta_content(k) = |L_c(k) - L_c(k-1)| <= eps_c; semantic convergence is D_global(k) <= eps_D, with both thresholds set empirically from tail fluctuations in the late-step window. Pre-RCP (Active Reasoning) is the disjunction of the two violations; Post-RCP (Converged Reasoning) is the conjunction of both conditions. The Reasoning Completion Point is k_RCP = min{k : Delta_content(k) <= eps_c AND D_global(k) <= eps_D}.

Because D_global requires multi-sample probing unavailable during ordinary decoding, k_RCP can only be computed offline, so the paper runs a 'distill-to-detect' pipeline. Offline, k_RCP is extracted per instance from full trajectories and treated as gold supervision. The key empirical bridge is that k_RCP typically coincides with the first emergence of the final answer, and that at that moment the rank R_k of the </think> token in the next-token distribution drops sharply -- a signal that is internal to the model and largely invariant to answer surface form (numbers, units, natural language, multiple-choice letters), unlike string matching on the answer itself. Using k_RCP on Math-500 as supervision, an interpretable decision tree is fit over R_k plus a short history of preceding rank values at sentence boundaries, then distilled into deterministic symbolic rules (Appendix C): immediate saturation C_sat: R_t <= 5; progressive convergence C_conv: R_{t-k} <= theta_k for k=0..3 with theta = [10, 50, 100, 1000]; short-term stability C_short: R_{t-k} <= 20 for k in {0,1,2}; long-term persistence C_long: R_{t-k} <= 50 for k in {0..5}. The stop signal is S_t = C_sat OR C_conv OR (C_short OR C_long). At inference RCPD applies these rules at each sentence boundary and, once triggered, forces </think> and transitions to answer generation. No training of the reasoning model is involved.

Evaluation uses each model's official chat template and delimiter format, nucleus sampling at temperature 0.6 / top-p 0.95, and a 32,768-token generation cap so behaviour is not driven by hard token limits. Efficiency is reported as Tok (mean generated tokens per instance, thinking plus content), Compression Rate CR = Tok/Tok_Full, and RPCR = (Acc - Acc_NoThink)/Tok * 10^4. The Budget Force baseline is given an oracle advantage: for each (model, benchmark) its budget is retrospectively selected so its average token usage matches RCPD's, a globally tuned budget the paper notes is not available at deployment time.

one_liner: Defines an instance-specific Reasoning Completion Point (RCP) as the earliest truncation step at which both content-length stabilization and semantic-distribution convergence hold, and detects it online by monitoring the rank of the </think> token, cutting tokens up to 44% while preserving accuracy across four Qwen3 scales and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B.
problem: Longer reasoning trajectories do not monotonically improve accuracy: excessive reasoning yields diminishing or negative returns (overthinking). What is missing is a fine-grained account of how each intermediate reasoning step influences the final answer, and therefore a principled boundary between reasoning that is still doing work and computation that is redundant. Because that boundary is latent and varies per instance, a fixed thinking-token budget cannot locate it, so mitigating overthinking has to be posed as an online detection problem during decoding.

relevance.overthinking: This is a direct, load-bearing contribution to the archive's central question. It gives the archive its most explicit operational definition of when reasoning has converged -- a conjunction of content-length stabilization and a KL residual against an estimated terminal semantic distribution -- and thereby separates the moment a trace converges from the moment the model actually stops, which is the quantity overthinking consists of. Two of its findings bear on mechanism rather than method: the rank of </think> drops sharply at answer emergence, meaning the model's own preference to terminate fires at convergence and is not acted on, which converges with separately archived work locating overthinking in a bias on the termination logit; and the counterfactual injection result (49 of 64 trials adopt an injected wrong intermediate answer) is direct evidence that post-convergence computation rationalizes earlier tokens instead of re-verifying them, which is a causal claim about why continuing past convergence is not merely wasteful but harmful. The iso-compute Budget Force comparison is also methodologically useful to the archive as a template: it makes the fixed-budget baseline strictly stronger than deployment allows, and still separates from it by 13 accuracy points at matched tokens.

results:
Benchmarks are AIME24 and AIME25 (30 problems each) and GPQA-Diamond (198 problems), on Qwen3-8B/14B/30B-A3B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B in Table 1, plus Qwen3-32B in Table 4.

Table 1 averages (Tok, CR, Acc, RPCR). Qwen3-8B: Full 14259 (100%) 65.22 27.22; No-Think 4998 (35%) 26.40 0.00; BF 8702 (61%) 56.66 34.77; DEER 13222 (93%) 66.53 30.35; RCPD 8052 (56%) 66.73 50.09. Qwen3-14B: Full 12591 (100%) 69.96 27.54; BF 7817 (62%) 57.80 28.80; DEER 11309 (90%) 68.90 29.72; RCPD 7498 (60%) 69.80 46.03. Qwen3-30B-A3B: Full 12472 (100%) 74.38 33.56; BF 9490 (76%) 68.27 37.66; DEER 11860 (95%) 71.87 33.17; RCPD 9457 (76%) 75.11 45.02. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B: Full 18704 (100%) 68.47 22.49; BF 14950 (80%) 63.55 24.85; DEER 18480 (99%) 66.08 21.47; RCPD 15465 (83%) 67.56 26.61. Table 4 (Qwen3-32B): Full 12063 (100%) 72.44 31.87; BF 8660 (72%) 66.48 37.52; DEER 11249 (93%) 72.49 34.23; RCPD 8358 (69%) 73.37 47.12.

So RCPD preserves average accuracy (8B +1.51, 14B -0.16, 30B-A3B +0.73, 32B +0.93, DeepSeek -0.91) and its compression is strongly model-dependent: the headline '44%' is the Qwen3-8B average (CR 56%), while DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B reaches only 17% reduction (CR 83%). The largest single-benchmark compression is Qwen3-8B on GPQA-D at CR 43%.

Against iso-compute Budget Force the gap is large at nearly matched budgets: Qwen3-8B AIME24, BF 10373 tokens at 58.88 accuracy versus RCPD 9958 tokens at 72.22. RCPD dominates both BF and DEER on every model average -- fewer tokens and equal-or-higher accuracy than BF, and far fewer tokens at equal-or-higher accuracy than DEER, which barely compresses (CR 90-99%).

This version reports a training-based S-GRPO baseline (results taken directly from that paper, only where available) which the paper concedes it does not beat everywhere: Qwen3-8B AIME24 S-GRPO 8810 tokens (57%) at 77.30 accuracy versus RCPD 9958 (65%) at 72.22; Qwen3-14B AIME24 S-GRPO 8932 (67%) at 77.90 versus RCPD 8799 (66%) at 73.33. On GPQA-D the ordering reverses: 8B S-GRPO 5271 (55%) at 55.40 versus RCPD 4130 (43%) at 64.65; 14B S-GRPO 4537 (59%) at 60.60 versus RCPD 3709 (48%) at 67.17. The text frames this as RCPD rivalling a training-based method without fine-tuning, outperforming S-GRPO on GPQA-D while underperforming on AIME24. AIME25 and average columns for S-GRPO are absent from the source paper and left blank.

GPQA-D accuracy rises under early exit on every Qwen3 model: 8B 60.10 -> 64.65, 14B 64.31 -> 67.17, 30B-A3B 66.50 -> 68.69, 32B 69.53 -> 71.21. It does not rise on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B (58.73 -> 58.25). The paper does not investigate the asymmetry.

Ablation (Table 2), stopping on a single rank threshold (</think> entering the top-5) rather than RCPD's temporal rules: Qwen3-8B 61.11 vs RCPD 75.11; Qwen3-14B 65.72 vs 69.79; Qwen3-30B-A3B 73.84 vs 75.11; Qwen3-32B 73.26 vs 73.37. The single-threshold rule is described as competitive but consistently worse, and the margin shrinks with scale.

Semantic convergence is quantified (Appendix D) by fitting a 95% confidence ellipse in the 2D PCA plane via squared Mahalanobis distance against chi-squared(0.95) = 5.991: 97.3% of post-RCP trajectory points fall inside the basin for the running example, 94.3% and 96.5% for two further AIME24 instances.

A counterfactual injection experiment (Appendix F, Table 3) tests whether post-RCP computation re-verifies. The initial tentative answer inside a reasoning trace is manually edited (12 -> 16) and 64 independent reasoning trials are run: 11 recover the original correct answer, 49 adopt the injected value, 4 produce something else. Flipping the injection (16 -> 12) gives 11 / 51 / 2. The paper reads this as strong confirmation bias -- post-RCP generation seldom performs genuine re-verification and instead rationalizes earlier tokens.
